newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEEGAN STUNS NEWCASTLE WITH SHOCK RESIGNATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEEGAN STUNS NEWCASTLE WITH SHOCK RESIGNATION.

text.p: Kevin Keegan shocked Newcastle United and the world of soccer on Wednesday by quitting as manager of the club he revitalised saying he no longer wanted to be a manager at this stage in his life.

Keegan, 45, who has transformed English premier league Newcastle in five years from a moribund sleeping giant into one of the most exciting teams in the country, had told the Newcastle board he wanted to quit at the end of the season but both parties agreed it would be better if he left immediately.
Keegan told Newcastle's Clubcall fan's telephone service: "It was my decision and my decision alone. I offered my resignation at the end of last season but was persuaded by the board to stay.
"I feel I have taken the club as far as I can and that it would be in the best interests of all concerned if I resigned."
Keegan's assistant Terry McDermott and coach Arthur Cox have assumed temporary control of first team affairs.

Newcastle director Douglas Hall said: "Kevin took over at the helm of a club destined for the second division and scaled the heights of the premier league with a style of football never before seen at St James' Park.
"Kevin leaves the club in a far stronger position than when he arrived and the squad of players he has built up is one of the strongest in Europe.
"The club wish to place on record their sincere appreciation of all Kevin has done for the club over the last five years."
The former Liverpool and England star took over at St James' Park in 1992 when Newcastle were near the bottom of the old second division.
After spending nearly 60 million pounds ($100 million) on players, Keegan took the club to almost the peak of the premier league, just losing out to Manchester United in last year's championship.
In the summer he signed England striker Alan Shearer for a world record 15 million pounds ($25 million).

A statement from the club read: "Newcastle United Football Club today announced the resignation of manager Kevin Keegan. Kevin informed the board of his wish to resign at the end of the season having decided he no longer wishes to continue in football management at this stage in his life.

"Following lengthy discussions at which the board tried to persuade Kevin to change his mind both parties agreed that the best route forward was for the club to reluctantly accept his resignation with immediate effect."

Newcastle are fourth in the table and through to the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup. They are still involved in the F.A. Cup but were knocked out of the League Cup by Middlesbrough in November. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
